control: wrong fact (CED 3.2.A.3.i: only the component of the force PARALLEL to the displacement changes the system's total energy; 3.2.A.3.ii says the perpendicular component does not change kinetic energy)
title: Which force component does work
body: Only the component of the force exerted on a system that is perpendicular to the displacement of the point of application will change the system's total energy.

control: wrong fact (CED 3.2.A.1.i: the work done by a CONSERVATIVE force is path-independent and depends only on the initial and final configurations)
title: Path dependence of work
body: The work done by a conservative force exerted on a system is path-dependent and changes with the route taken between the initial and final configurations.

control: wrong owner topic (power is topic 3.5, EK 3.5.A.1-2; 3.2 is the work done by a force)
title: Average power
body: Average power is the amount of energy transferred or converted divided by the time it took for that transfer or conversion to occur.

control: swapped graph relationships (CED 3.2.A.5: work is the area under a graph of force as a function of displacement, not its slope)
title: Work from a force-displacement graph
body: Work is equal to the slope of a graph of force as a function of displacement.

control: hook expansion contradicts the CED (3.4.C.2: mechanical energy is constant when the work done on the system is zero AND there are no nonconservative interactions). The entry is correct, so only the hook should be rejected.
title: When total mechanical energy is constant
body: If the work done on a selected system is zero and there are no nonconservative interactions within the system, the total mechanical energy of the system is constant.

expands_to.means: the total mechanical energy of any selected system
stays constant regardless of the work done on it or nonconservative interactions

hooks.when_to_use: when deciding whether mechanical energy is constant
hooks.caution: State the conditions in CED terms when answering.
